instruction: Increase the text scaling factor to 1.25 for better readability on this display.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened terminal, navigated to GNOME Terminal Preferences, created 'LargeTerminal' profile with 132 columns and 43 rows, but failed to set it as default profile. Spent remaining turns struggling with gsettings commands to change default profile ID.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open applications via Activities search, navigate GNOME Terminal Preferences UI, create/modify terminal profiles, run terminal commands (stty, dconf, gsettings), interact with GNOME desktop settings
metadata.failure_analysis: Model created the profile correctly but could not set it as default. Used wrong command ('settings' instead of 'gsettings'), struggled with profile ID management, and ran out of turns (50).
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a single accessibility setting change (text scaling). Model demonstrated ability to interact with GNOME settings; this tests a straightforward gsettings modification without complex profile management.
metadata.explanation: Task requires increasing GNOME text scaling factor to 1.25. Evaluator runs 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface text-scaling-factor' and custom metric check_text_scaling compares output against expected_factor 1.25 with tolerance 0.01. Achievable via Settings > Accessibility or gsettings command. [Fixed: replaced official check_text_enlarged (1-param signature) with custom 2-param metric that properly compares against expected_factor from rules]
fix_history: Fix 1: Replaced official check_text_enlarged metric (1-param, only checks >1.0) with custom check_text_scaling__04c87fb26c99f62f08868d28d96db622 metric (2-param) that compares scaling factor against expected_factor with abs tolerance 0.01
Fix 2: Updated new_functions_paths to include the new custom metric file
Fix 3: Updated explanation to document the fix

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface text-scaling-factor' via vm_command_line to extract the exact setting the instruction requires.
Custom metric correctly handles the expected parameter: accesses expected.get('expected_factor') directly from the rules dict, consistent with the framework's get_rule behavior for type='rule'.
Expected value 1.25 exactly matches the instruction requirement.
Metric correctly parses the gsettings string output to float, strips whitespace, and compares with 0.01 tolerance — appropriate for floating-point comparison.
Complete coverage: the instruction has a single requirement (set text scaling to 1.25) and the evaluator fully verifies it.
Error handling is robust: handles dict error results, non-string inputs, and parsing failures gracefully by returning 0.0.
